description: Given two non-empty lists of integers a and b, each sorted in non-decreasing order, return the smallest absolute difference |a[i] - b[j]| over all pairs of an element of a and an element of b. The result is a non-negative integer and must be attained by some pair.
notes: The existential (some pair attains the result) is stated in Dafny with the recursive predicate DistanceOccursFrom ({:fuel 10}): some x in a has x - result or x + result in b, which is equivalent to |x - y| == result for some y in b because result >= 0. Dafny cannot find the witness pair of an existential on concrete inputs. The Python spec keeps VERINA's form.
